transcript:
>> This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
>> Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder.
House Republicans have beaten back an effort to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.
The House Tuesday voted 211 to 204 to effectively block impeachment charges from being considered.
Earlier in the day, Hegseth held his first press conference at the Pentagon in six months.
Here's David Fochenflick.
>> I'd say he was tense and intense.
And what was clear is throughout his remarks, he wrapped himself in President Trump and
in the troops as though he was their shield and their protector.
Here's a sound bite of what I mean.
>> Put the secretary on trial today and the men and women who carried out those orders
tomorrow.
If they want to come for the warriors, they're going to have to come through me.
>> That seemed like an inversion of what was happening.
He wanted to use them to shield him.
>> House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries says Democrats will have a conversation about
impeaching Hegseth when they take control of Congress in January.
Jeffries is expected to become the next House Speaker.
Republicans meanwhile have elected Congressman Jim Jordan to be their leader and appears Claudia
Grisales reports on Jordan's election to the top party post Tuesday.
>> House Republicans elected Ohio Congressman Jim Jordan leader after House Speaker Mike
Johnson said he would step down after last week's midterm election losses.
After the win, Jordan shared some of his plans for the new job.
>> Over the next two years, House Republicans will fight for American families.
When Democrats offer more government, we'll offer more freedom and we will bring that
fight in committee on the floor and on the stump every single day.
>> The House Judiciary Committee chair beat the number two House Republican, Steve Scalise,
to win the minority leadership role.
>> Johnson told his colleagues his conference hasn't had a, quote, clear plan to survive
the hour or day in front of us, but that would change under his leadership.
Claudia Grisales, NPR News.
>> Russian and Ukrainian officials have wrapped up their first day of US sponsor peace talks
in Abu Dhabi.
The first meeting since February comes amid a new push for a broader peace deal, NPR's
Charles Maines reports.
Talks went for about four hours and pick up again Wednesday, but neither the US, Russian,
nor Ukrainian delegations have commented directly on their progress.
Yet Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Ukrainian President Vladimir Zelensky suggested the
talks had been constructed thus far.
The Abu Dhabi meeting comes shortly after President Trump hosted a senior Kremlin envoy at the
White House, after which Trump suggested a wider peace deal involving Europe was within
reach.
US officials speaking on background say their focus is on creating a new security architecture
between Russia and Europe, believing that could unlock concessions from both Kiev and
Moscow than the actual fighting.
Charles Maines, NPR News, Moscow.
>> And you're listening to NPR News.
Among the many upsets last week, Democrats flipped a pivotal House seat in California,
as Jackie Fortier with KFF Health News reports, Medicaid helped tip the race.
>> For years, dairy farmer David Valadeo was a Republican voice from California's Central
Valley in Congress.
But last week, voters swept him out of office.
Jeff Cummins is a political science professor at California State University, Fresno.
>> He just had a perfect storm against Valadeo, the national political environment, high inflation,
and then his votes in Congress.
>> Valadeo voted for the big budget bill that cuts Medicaid by more than $900 billion.
He made that decision even though 6 in 10 people in his district get their health care
through Medicaid.
Democrat Randy Villegas was the clear winner.
He ran on a platform of universal health care.
>> That's Jackie Fortier with our partner KFF Health News.
Vote counting is ongoing in outstanding Senate races in Mississippi and Alaska, where Democrat
Mary Peltola increased her lead Tuesday, Alaska Public Media, reporting that election
officials have counted more than 24,000 additional votes.
And Peltola leads a Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan 49% to 47%.
In Mississippi, Democrat Scott Colombe holds a narrow lead over Republican incumbent Cindy
Hyde Smith.
The artificial intelligence company Anthropic is seeking a roughly $1.3 trillion valuation
in its initial public offering.
Because the AI company behind the Claude chatbot, it said in a regulatory filing Tuesday that
it will offer 825 million shares.
This is NPR News.

topics.text: House Republicans defeat effort to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, 211-204 vote
Hegseth holds first Pentagon press conference in six months, defends troops and Trump
Hakeem Jeffries says Democrats will consider impeaching Hegseth when they control Congress in January
House Republicans elect Jim Jordan as leader after Mike Johnson steps down
Russian and Ukrainian officials conclude first day of US-sponsored peace talks in Abu Dhabi
Democrat Randy Villegas flips California House seat held by Republican David Valadao, Medicaid a factor
Democrat Mary Peltola extends lead over Republican Dan Sullivan in Alaska Senate race
Democrat Scott Colombe holds narrow lead over Republican Cindy Hyde Smith in Mississippi Senate race
AI company Anthropic seeks roughly $1.3 trillion valuation in initial public offering
